metaDescription: Six wooden table lamps compared on solid wood versus wood-look bases, height, tripod stability, shades and touch controls, with honest notes on finish and fit.
expertTake: The EDISHINE 22 in walnut lamp is the best overall pick because it combines a solid walnut base, a non-slip pad and a standard E26 socket at a fair cost tier. The 13.4 in EDISHINE is the value pick for a small nightstand. Skip the category if you want a lamp that never shows a mark, because wood scratches and finishes wear where hands lift it.
introParagraphs: A wooden lamp base brings warmth that glass, ceramic and metal do not. Grain and tone add texture to a nightstand or a side table, and a wood base pairs easily with a linen shade, leather and woven fabrics.

Listings blur the line between solid wood, veneer, painted wood-look surfaces and resin, so the first job is to find out what the base really is. This guide compares six lamps on material, height, stability and shade, and says plainly where a lamp is wood and where it only looks like it.

products.name: EDISHINE 22 in farmhouse lamp with tapered solid walnut base and beige linen shade

specList.label: Socket
specList.value: E26 with on and off switch

products.description:
This EDISHINE is a 22 in lamp with a tapered base in solid walnut, topped by a beige linen shade. The listing describes natural grain details and a non-slip pad on the base for stability on a nightstand. A standard E26 socket and an on and off switch keep it simple.

The tradeoff is that solid wood shows scratches and dents more easily than a metal or glass base, and the tapered shape means the foot is smaller than the top. Compared with the tripod lamps in this lineup, it stands taller and looks more traditional, but the tripods have a wider footprint. At 22 in it is a good size for a bedside table that is about 24 to 28 in high.

In ownership terms, assembly is minimal: fit the shade and a bulb. Use an LED at or below the rated wattage so the linen does not scorch, and wipe the wood with a dry or lightly damp cloth, never a wet one. Keep it out of direct sun, which can fade walnut over years. A small amount of furniture wax or a drop of oil on a soft cloth, applied once a year, revives the grain and fills hairline scratches, but check the maker's finish first, because a lacquered surface needs no oil and may streak if you add one. Position the lamp so the cord leaves the back of the table, not across the front edge.
products.bestFor: Bedsides and side tables that want a real wood base in a classic height.

Non-slip pad adds stability on a nightstand
Standard E26 socket allows any compatible bulb
22 in height suits most bedside tables
cons: Wood scratches and dents more easily than metal or glass
Tapered base has a smaller footprint than a tripod

products.name: EDISHINE 13.4 in small solid wood table lamp with beige linen shade
products.description:
The 13.4 in EDISHINE is a compact lamp with a clean, natural, minimalist style, a solid wood base and a soft beige linen shade. The listing notes that the solid wood adds weight to prevent tipping and that the small size saves space. An E26 base and an on and off switch keep the hardware standard.

The tradeoff is scale: at 13.4 in it is a small lamp for a narrow nightstand or a shelf, and it will not light a page from across a bed. Compared with the 22 in lamp, it is much shorter and gives less spread. It is a good accent lamp and a good second lamp for a room.

In ownership terms, use a small LED bulb with a warm tone, and keep the shade a few inches from curtains. Wipe the wood with a dry cloth. It suits a small bedside table, a bookshelf or a desk. Used as a pair on a wide dresser, two small lamps create a gentle wash of light along the wall, and the weighted base means a hand brushing past in the dark is less likely to send one over. Match the bulb colour across lamps so one does not look yellow beside the other.
products.bestFor: Small nightstands, shelves and desks that need a compact wooden accent lamp.
pros: Compact 13.4 in size fits narrow tables and shelves
Solid wood base is weighted to resist tipping
Soft linen shade diffuses warm light
Lower cost tier among the real-wood lamps
cons: Small size gives limited light for reading in bed

products.name: EDISHINE 14.2 in tripod table lamp, light brown wooden base, beige linen shade
products.description:
The EDISHINE tripod has a light brown wooden three-leg base and a beige linen shade at 14.2 in tall. The triangular stand gives a wider footprint than a single column, and the listing says it is robust and not easy to tip. Light brown wood suits scandi and modern rooms.

The tradeoff is that a tripod takes more table width than a column, so it needs a roomy nightstand, and legs can be bumped. Compared with the solid walnut 22 in lamp, it is smaller and lighter in tone. A tripod also leaves air under the shade, which looks airy but exposes the cord path.

In ownership terms, check that all three legs sit flat, and tighten the screws if they loosen. Keep the lamp on a stable surface, with the cord tucked behind. It suits a bedside or a console where a light, open look is wanted. Because the legs splay outwards, the lamp takes a wider square on the table than its shade suggests, so measure the tabletop before you buy. A lamp pad or a small dish of keys beside it will not crowd the legs if you leave about two inches around each foot.
products.bestFor: Scandi and modern bedsides that want a stable tripod base in a light wood tone.
pros: Wooden tripod gives a stable, wide footprint
Light brown tone suits scandi and modern rooms
Open legs look airy and light
Standard E26 base takes any compatible bulb
cons: Tripod takes more table width than a single column

products.name: GOEBLESON 14.6 in tripod table lamp, wood legs, beige linen shade
products.description:
The GOEBLESON is a 14.6 in tripod lamp with wood legs and a high-density linen shade, described as mid-century modern with a minimalist design. The listing says the structure is more stable and less likely to tip than a single-column lamp. The dense linen diffuses a soft, warm glow.

The tradeoff is that its look is close to the EDISHINE tripod, so the choice depends on tone and shade. Compared with the 22 in solid walnut lamp, it is much shorter. A mid-century shape suits retro rooms but may look small in a large living room.

In ownership terms, assemble the legs carefully and check for wobble. Use a warm LED and keep the shade clear of curtains. It suits a nightstand or a small side table. If you read in bed, add a taller lamp elsewhere in the room, because a 14 in tripod puts its bulb below a seated reader's eye line and throws light up to the ceiling rather than onto the page. As a night light, though, its gentle glow is exactly right.
products.bestFor: Retro bedrooms that want a mid-century tripod on a small nightstand.

High-density linen shade diffuses light evenly

Compact size fits a nightstand

products.name: 23.5 in modern wood table lamps set of 2, walnut, solid wood bases with linen shades
products.description:
This set of two 23.5 in lamps has solid wood bases in a walnut tone and premium linen shades. The neutral hues are meant to match most room palettes, and the matching pair suits symmetrical bedsides or a console. The listing says the bases are made of solid wood.

The tradeoff is that a pair doubles the footprint and needs two outlets, and a tall lamp needs a wide enough table. Compared with the single 22 in EDISHINE, you get two lamps for one purchase, but with less brand history. The shades are plain linen, so the style relies on the wood tone.

In ownership terms, assemble both, then check both are the same height on the table. Use matching bulbs, and keep both shades clean. It suits a bedroom with two nightstands or a sofa with two end tables. Before you hang a shade or fit a bulb, stand both bases side by side and check that the grain and tone are close, since solid wood varies from piece to piece and a pair can look slightly mismatched. A quick rotation of one lamp on its pad often hides a difference in grain direction.
products.bestFor: Bedrooms and sofas that need a matched pair of solid wood lamps.
pros: Two matching solid wood lamps in one set
23.5 in height suits most bedside tables
Neutral linen shade matches most palettes
Walnut tone is warm without being dark
cons: Two lamps need two outlets and wide enough tables

products.name: 16.1 in touch table lamp, wood-painted body, 3-way dimmable, bulb included
products.description:
This 16.1 in lamp has a body with a wood-painted finish and a touch control: tap anywhere on the body to cycle three brightness levels. A dimmable LED bulb comes in the box. The listing says to touch the lamp's body to adjust the brightness, which suits a bedside in the dark.

The tradeoff is that the body is wood-painted, which means a painted surface rather than a true natural grain, so it will not age like solid wood. Compared with the solid wood lamps, it is more practical but less authentic. Touch controls can misread near other metal or static.

In ownership terms, keep the body dry and use the bulb supplied, since a non-dimmable bulb will not work with the touch circuit. Wipe with a dry cloth. It suits a bedside where touch control and a wood look are wanted at a modest cost. Touch lamps can behave oddly on a metal nightstand, so test it on the actual table, and if it flickers on its own, a felt pad under the base often breaks the contact. Treat the painted finish as you would a painted shelf: avoid solvents and abrasive pads.
products.bestFor: Bedsides that want touch dimming and a wood look without a wood price.

buyingCriteria.explanation: Solid wood has real grain, takes repair and ages gracefully, but costs more and can scratch. Wood-painted bodies, veneers and resin with a wood-grain finish look similar in photos but behave differently. One listing in this category states plainly that its lamp is resin, not real wood. Read the material line and the word solid. A quick weight check also helps once the lamp arrives: a solid wood base feels dense and cool, while a hollow resin or painted composite feels light for its size. Neither is wrong if the listing is honest, but you should know which you are paying for.

A bedside lamp is usually 20 to 26 in tall, and the bottom of the shade should be near eye level when seated in bed. Small 13 to 16 in lamps are accent lamps. The shade should be about two thirds of the lamp's height. The 22 in and 23.5 in lamps cover most bedside tables, while the 14 in lamps suit shelves.

A tripod spreads weight over three feet and resists tipping, while a tapered single column has a small foot. A non-slip pad helps on polished tables. Check the width of your table against the footprint. Wooden legs can loosen, so tighten the screws after a few weeks.

A linen shade diffuses light and softens glare, while thicker linen cuts more light. A beige or white shade gives a warm glow. Use LED bulbs, since a hot bulb can scorch fabric and dry the wood near the socket. A 400 to 800 lumen bulb suits most bedsides.

A simple on and off switch is the most reliable, while touch controls add dimming but can misfire. Dimming needs a compatible bulb. A lamp with a bulb included saves a purchase, but check the bulb type.

Oiled or lacquered wood wipes clean with a dry cloth, while painted finishes can chip. Keep wood away from sun, which fades tone, and from damp, which can swell joints. Light scratches are a feature of real wood.

faq.q: How do I tell solid wood from wood-look?
faq.a: Read the material line. Words such as solid, walnut or oak suggest real wood, while wood-grain finish, painted or resin suggest a look-alike.
Yes, softer woods can scratch and dent. A pad under the base and gentle handling help.

faq.q: What bulb is best for a wooden lamp?
faq.a: A warm 2700K LED at or below the socket rating. LEDs run cooler, which protects linen and wood.
They spread weight over three feet and resist tipping, but they need more table width.

faq.q: How tall should a bedside lamp be?
faq.a: Usually 20 to 26 in, so the shade bottom is near eye level when seated in bed.

faq.q: Can I clean a wooden lamp with water?
faq.a: Only with a barely damp cloth, dried at once. Water can stain and swell wood.
